description: A shift register of random bits that loops as a sequence, giving a stepped voltage and a trigger, with thirty-two stored patterns

params.text: Sets what happens to the bit entering the register on each clock: centred makes it random, fully clockwise locks the loop, and moving left of centre doubles the loop length with the same chances
Sets how many steps the loop runs, up to 16, and up to 32 with the CTRL knob left of centre
Forces the next bit entering the register to be off
Forces the next bit entering the register to be on
Randomises every bit in the register at once
Selects one of the thirty-two stored patterns, 0 to 31; the choice only takes effect when SET is pressed, unless AUTO is on
Loads the selected pattern, even after randomisation has changed it
Double-click to store the current sequence and its length into the selected pattern
Applies a pattern change the moment it is made, instead of waiting for the SET button

inputs.text: Moves the CTRL setting, added to the CTRL knob
A trigger here does what the DEL button does
A trigger here does what the ADD button does
Advances the register one step on each trigger
A trigger here restarts the sequence from its beginning
A trigger here clears the register, turning every bit off
A trigger here does what the RND button does
Selects the pattern by voltage, or steps to the next stored one on each trigger with Prog Input type set to Trig
A trigger here does what the RECL button does

outputs.text: A 1ms pulse each time the sequence advances onto an on bit, or a gate or a clock-width pulse under Trig Output type
The voltage built from the on bits of the register, attenuated by the SCALE knob

notes: every bit off gives 0V and every bit on gives 10V; each bit position is worth a different amount, doubling as you go by default.
a pattern is only saved by double-clicking STOR; randomising and moving on loses it.
menu: Buffered Del/Add — makes one press of DEL or ADD affect only the next bit, instead of holding while the button is down
Buffered Random — makes one press of RND randomise once, instead of holding while the button is down
Math Settings — a submenu holding Bit Resolution and Voltage progression
Bit Resolution: 8 bit, 16 bit — sets how many of the register's bits the output voltage is built from
Voltage progression: 2x (std.), 1.3x, Fibonacci — sets how much each further bit is worth in the output voltage
Trig Output type: Trig, Gate, Clock Width — chooses whether an on bit sends a 1ms pulse, a gate held until an off bit, or a pulse the length of the incoming clock's high part
Ignore Prog Ctrl — leaves the CTRL knob alone when a pattern is recalled, instead of restoring the stored setting
Ignore Prog Scale — leaves the SCALE knob alone when a pattern is recalled, instead of restoring the stored setting
Don't advance — makes the first clock after a reset hold on the first step rather than moving off it
Prog Input type: CV, Trig — chooses whether the PROG jack reads a voltage or steps to the next stored pattern on each trigger
Scan Last Prog — reads every pattern again and reports the highest one that holds anything
Copy Sequence — puts the current sequence on a clipboard shared with trigSeq modules
Paste Sequence — takes a sequence off that clipboard; it is shown as a plain label when the clipboard is empty
DISK operations — a submenu with Load Preset and Save Preset for all thirty-two patterns, and Import and Export trigSeq seq. for the working sequence
Erase ALL progs — clears every stored pattern, behind an 'Are you Sure?' submenu whose only item is ERASE!
Initialize on Start — clears the register when Rack loads a patch, without erasing the stored patterns
Tips — a submenu that only prints reminders about storing patterns with a double-click
